items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1969-12-04
items.q: I played a show one night for the Kiwanis club and they had Al Streeman. Now I love Al, he's a great guy, nice fella.

ctx.x: I'm just wondering if you ever played many things for churches, you know, you mentioned being a mason. For the Shriners? Yeah. Well I played the Muslim ball every year.

I played all the Masonic balls and many others that were not Masonic. I played Clough Knight Revelers, Proteus, Harlekins. I played on the average of thirty-five carnival balls a season. Get through at twelve o'clock and rush to the hotel and play one to four and then have rehearsal next morning, nine o'clock and everybody's knocked out and they're in a bad humor. Captain Donoghé, one note from the other. I used to have to tell them, who's the musician here, you or me? I can get enough of them. Then they say he's…
Then he gives me a $100 tip.

items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1973-03-16
items.q: Al Streeman goes there. Al Streeman is the guy that sets up the band with white gloves on.

ctx.x: The first thing he'd do is say, why are you all drinking? You know what I mean? And Cuny didn't drink. And Cuny used to be the reason why we used to, when we played on the courthouse steps during the Spring Fiesto, I had a big band, Fakin' in the dark, you know. Oh, come the way, it's a trip. You can't forget this, you know. A man said to me, he said, your piano player, he's on the piano more than he's on top of it. I said he's repairing the pedals now, he just got through with the keys. He tuned the piano. He…
